artifact_revision: agentmux 9f989606 + session-14 working tree (amx 0.8.0, revision 9f989606b1fd-dirty, built from it into an isolated bin; Agent Mux.app Debug built from it by `just mac-app`, run as a copy under bundle identifier io.github.sglavoie.agentmux.acceptance14); embedded Ghostty 1.3.1; tmux 3.7c on AgentMux's private server; installed asl; macOS 27
method: One recorded live run on this machine in an isolated world under /tmp/amxs14 (own HOME, TMPDIR, config, daemon, runtime-session registry, private tmux server, app preferences domain). The world has no Kitty: none is started, no process is given a Kitty socket, and the world's daemon reports kitty_snapshot.ready=False throughout. The real app is driven through System Events accessibility (window, sidebar, main menu, status menu), real CGEvent clicks, and typed keys; its unified log is read with `log show`. The utility views' screens are read and their keys sent through an observer tmux on its own socket, which the amx shim hosts each `amx workspace-view` in with exactly the environment the app's terminal gave it; agent terminals (`amx attach`) are not wrapped. 145 checks, 0 failed (desktop-acceptance.log ends 'RESULT: 0 check(s) failed'). Two earlier full passes are not the record: one stopped after the driver's row selection stuck at the end of the list, and one had 3 failed checks that were the driver's (two expected one of two valid log lines for a released terminal, one mouse click landed before the app was frontmost); the driver was corrected and the whole run repeated from a rebuilt world. Stand-ins, stated plainly: the harness is a shell script named claude (no model, no network) that prints its identity, sends real hooks through `amx hook-indicator` on typed commands, and as an `asl run` worker holds one turn open; the editor is a script that prints what it was asked to edit. Real: the app, embedded Ghostty, tmux, the amx dashboard/overview/workspace-view/attach/hook client/daemon, the registry, Git worktrees, and the installed asl. Not exercised live: a real Claude/Codex/Copilot agent; the global dashboard shortcut and the status menu's Launch Project with no Kitty (the operator's own Kitty runs on this machine with a socket at the default address, which the app would rightly try first; their routing is covered by hosted tests DashboardOpener.destination and ProjectCatalog.workspaceLaunchArguments); the TUI's fall back to its own terminal when no workspace is connected (covered by Go tests). Three screenshots that caught a window of the operator's desktop in front of the app were deleted unpublished and two were retaken after the run with the app in front; the log's last section says so.

dashboard-launch-focus.evidence: Observed in session-14/desktop-acceptance.log (cases fresh, env, launch, focus). The app opened its workspace on a Dashboard view whose terminal runs `amx workspace-view dashboard`: the existing TUI, listing the tmux session beta, with the app as the one daemon subscriber reporting workspace_views=True. Launching alpha from the TUI's launcher registered one new live tmux runtime session; the app logged 'awaiting just-launched session', then 'awaited session ... is listed; showing it' and 'attached a terminal to' that ID; the window title became 'alpha — work', the sidebar selection moved to the alpha row, exactly one client was attached to alpha's pane, and the Dashboard kept running behind it listing both sessions. A line typed into the app reached alpha's agent, whose PermissionRequest hook then showed as 'needs attention' on its sidebar row and '1 waiting' on its project. Enter on the beta row in the TUI produced 'view request for session <beta>' in the app, a terminal attached by the workspace, title 'beta — work', one client on beta's pane, alpha still attached, and the dashboard process with no child of its own (it attached nothing itself). Enter on alpha again returned to its existing view with no second attachment. Screenshots: launch-attention.png, focus-native-view.png, dashboard-view.png. Daemon forwarding and validation: internal/daemon TestWorkspaceView* (go-test.log); app side: WorkspaceViewsWindowTests (xcodebuild-test.log, exit 0).

shell-editor-pager-overview.evidence: Observed in session-14/desktop-acceptance.log (cases overview, pager, shell, editor). View > Overview started `amx workspace-view overview` as its own sidebar view with a tile per tmux session and no client attached by previewing; Enter on a tile sent a view request and the window moved to that session's native view while the Overview kept running. Peek scrollback from the Dashboard's action menu opened a pager view ('alpha, pager view' under Workspace) showing less at (END) with the line the agent had printed, attached nothing, did not suspend the Dashboard, and on q ended and returned the pane to the Dashboard with its row gone. Open shell opened 'alpha, shell view' running a login shell in /tmp/amxs14/proj/alpha. Open editor opened 'alpha, editor view' running the configured editor on that path, and closed with it. The same views opened from the Worktrees view (shell in the managed worktree) and the Plans view (editor on the plan directory) in the workflows case. Screenshots: overview-view.png, pager-view.png, shell-view.png, editor-view.png.

utility-identity-isolation.evidence: Observed in session-14/desktop-acceptance.log (case isolation). The app was started with AMX_RUNTIME_SESSION_ID set to the live session beta plus KITTY_WINDOW_ID=999 and CLAUDECODE=1; the shim log shows every view's terminal inherited them. Inside the shell view `env` counted 0 identity variables (IDENTITY_VARS=0), and the editor reported 0 as well. A harness started by hand in the shell view printed 'runtime session: none  kitty window: none' and sent a PermissionRequest hook; afterwards the daemon snapshot still listed the same two sessions, attention.total was still 0, beta was untouched, the registry had the same records, the private tmux server the same panes, and the sidebar counted nothing waiting. Control: the same hook from a process that did carry beta's identity marked beta icon=key attention=True. The status menu listed the two sessions and no utility view; with alpha waiting and the shell view selected, the next-attention shortcut left the view and focused alpha's native view. Exiting the shell ended its view with both agents still attached. Also: cmd/dashboard TestWorkspaceShell*/Editor*/Pager*/Surfaces* (go-test.log) and WorkspaceViewsWindowTests.testUtilityViewsAreNeverSessionsAndNeverWait (xcodebuild-test.log).
